_readme: SafeFile JP content guard rules — the SINGLE source for the writing rules that
can be checked mechanically. Strategy v3.1 §3-1 and §3-4.
Two engines read this file and must agree:
* scripts/content/make_episode.mjs  (Mac, before the assets are written)
* app/services/jp_content_guard.rb  (server, on every content:jp_import)
Before S8 the two lived apart: make_episode.mjs held the list as JS constants
and the server had no check at all. Cross-review Q4 asked for one source,
because a rule enforced in one place and trusted in the other is a rule that
exists in one place — the exact way ep01 shipped 「複数枚をまとめて読み込めます」
with a clean build (the guard was reading only the Japanese body at the time).
Patterns are plain strings compiled by BOTH JavaScript RegExp and Ruby Regexp,
so they must stay inside the syntax both accept. Flags are declared as fields
rather than written inline ((?i) is Ruby-only, and dotall is `s` in JS but `m`
in Ruby): use "ignorecase": true and "dotall": true. Lookbehind is used in
one place (legal_claim #4) and is supported by both engines; both loaders
compile every pattern at startup, so an unportable one fails loudly on the
next run instead of silently never matching.
Rules that a regex cannot decide. They are listed in scripts/content/README.md
under a separate heading so that «there is a rule» and «the rule is enforced»
do not look the same: a first-person victim account (the pattern below catches
one shape of it, not the idea), and the ≤800px reduced-illustration rule for
dummy documents (no episode carries an illustration, so nothing fires it).

must_line.ja: 提出先の指示を必ず確認してください
must_line.ja_sentence: 提出先の指示を必ず確認してください。
_note: The Japanese form must appear as its OWN LINE and must end in 「。」.
Cross-review Q4 asked for the punctuation to be part of the rule: a line
that trails off mid-sentence, or one buried inside a paragraph, reads as
copy rather than as the standing instruction it is.
tweet_weighted (280) is X's actual limit under twitter-text weighting: CJK
counts 2, Latin 1, any URL a flat 23, and an emoji ZWJ sequence 2 for the
whole cluster. tweet_editorial (140) is OUR house limit, not the platform's
— v3 called 140 «X's limit», which cross-review Q3 corrected. The guard
fails on tweet_editorial so threads stay readable, and says which number it
is failing on; a tweet over 280 is impossible to post at all.
linkedin_chars lived here until S9 and now lives in linkedin.limits.chars,
next to the other LinkedIn rules. It was never checked in two places by
intent — it just ended up that way, and a number with two homes is a number
that gets changed in one of them.

forbidden.why: 事件名 — 戦略が名指しを禁じている / incident name, the strategy forbids naming it
「絶対」は断定 — 「原則」「リスクを下げる」を使う
「唯一」は断定
「必ず安全」は断定
「完全に」は断定 — 「読み取れなくする」に置き換える
「防ぐ」は活用形すべて禁止(防ぐ/防ぎます/防げます/防いで/防がない…) — 「リスクを下げる」を使う
forbidden._note: Cross-review Q4: the old rule listed 防ぎます|防げます only, so 「防ぐ」「防いで」「防げる」 walked past it. 防 followed by one of ぐぎげがごい is the verb; 防止・防犯・消防・予防する are followed by other characters and do not match.

forbidden.why: 一括処理は未出荷 — 宣伝しない

forbidden.re: 複数(枚|ファイル|のPDF|PDF|書類をまとめ)
forbidden.why: 複数ファイル入力は未出荷 — ファイル入力は1件のみ

forbidden.re: まとめて(読み込|処理|ダウンロード|黒塗り)
forbidden.why: 複数ファイル入力は未出荷
処理ログはチームプランのロードマップ項目で、出荷済み機能ではない
「先着N社」は数えていないカウントダウン — 有料プランがまだ存在せず、割り引く元の価格もない。「先行利用の事務所を募集しています（無料）」を使う
forbidden._note: Added S11 (2026-11-02). The outreach playbook §2 had this on its forbidden list before the first mail went out, and the nyusatsu landing was still saying it — a rule that lived in one document and was enforced nowhere. No episode has ever carried the phrase (grepped), so this fires on nothing today and exists to stop it coming back.

forbidden.re: 保存して(共有|おく)|共有リンク
forbidden.why: 保存・共有リンクは未出荷
batch processing has not shipped

forbidden.re: several files|multiple files|all at once|at once is fine|in one pass|in bulk
forbidden.why: multi-file input has not shipped
the processing log has not shipped

forbidden.re: 制限されています|禁止されています|違法です|義務づけられています|原則として制限されて
forbidden.why: 法的効果を断定している — 上限は「制限される場合があります」

forbidden.re: is restricted|is prohibited|is illegal|law constrains|are required by law
forbidden.why: asserts current legal effect; the cap is "may be restricted"
「あなた」は使わない — 主語を省略するか「提出する側」「担当者」
1人称ブランド話法は禁止 — 「SafeFile」または無主語
brand first-person / sales voice is forbidden on LinkedIn too

forbidden.re: 私の.{0,40}(免許証|保険証|住民票|マイナンバー).{0,60}(流出|漏えい|漏洩|晒され)
forbidden.why: 1人称の被害談 — 戦略が書くことを禁じている
forbidden._note: A heuristic: it catches one SHAPE (a personal leak told as having happened to the author) and nothing else. It does not replace reading the draft — see scripts/content/README.md.

_note: Cross-review Q4: «every article must carry a 施行日» invites hallucination.
A 手順 article about dragging a file onto a page has no legal claim to source,
and forcing one produces a citation nobody checked.
So the rule is conditional: IF the text makes a claim about what the law
requires or restricts, THEN the same article must carry a primary source on a
*.go.jp host AND the date it was confirmed. If it makes no such claim it
passes untouched. The point is to stop unsourced legal assertions, not to get
a URL into every post — and a go.jp host passing a regex is NOT verification;
it only means a human had to put a checkable address next to the claim.

claim_patterns.re: (が|を)(?:法令上)?求められ(て|ます|る|た)
claim_patterns.why: 「求められる」は法的要求の主張
「制限される」は法的効果の主張

claim_patterns.re: 義務(が|を|です|づけ|化|です)
(?<![方手用療文語作寸魔話漢])法(第[0-9０-９]+条|の規定|に基づ|により定め|上の)

claim_patterns.why: 告示・省令・政令の名指し

claim_patterns.re: \b(Health Insurance Act|National Health Insurance Act|Act on Prevention of Transfer of Criminal Proceeds|Personal Information Protection Act|My Number Act)\b
\b(in force since|came into force|takes effect on|effective from)\b
claim_patterns.why: asserts an enforcement date in English
asserts a legal requirement or restriction in English

_en_note: The English patterns exist because post_en.md is a parallel rewrite, not a
translation — it carries the same legal claim in its own words, and the
Japanese patterns above can never match it. Without these four, an English
article could assert what a statute requires with no source at all and the
guard would report nothing. They are deliberately narrow (named statutes,
enforcement-date phrasings, «may be restricted», «Article N») rather than
keyword-ish, because a false positive here pushes an author to bolt a
citation onto a sentence that did not need one.
legal_claim.why: 法的主張があるのに、同じ記事に *.go.jp の原文URLと「確認日: YYYY-MM-DD」がない

_note: 1ツイート目の1行目のルール — マーケティング計画 §6-1(2026-10-27):
「最初の一行は常に相手の痛み」。機能・「無料」・ブランド名で始めない。
── 正規表現で決められること / 決められないこと ──────────────────────
「痛みで始まっているか」は正規表現が判定できない。判定できるのは、痛みでは
ありえない『形』だけ — 統計・解説の枠組み(〜の多くは/原因です)、機能や無料
からの書き出し、ブランド名での主語。だからここにあるのは FORBIDDEN だけで、
「痛みで書けているか」は人が読む(scripts/content/README.md の二表)。
この規則は X の1ツイート目の1行目にだけ当たる。同じ文を記事のリードに書くのは
まったく問題ない — 記事は読みに来た人が読み、ツイートは流れていく人の目に
止まらなければならない、という違いだけが理由である。

_max_chars_note: 全角・半角を区別しない素の文字数。痛みの一行は短い — 長くなるのは説明を
始めたときで、その意味で長さは『解説になっていないか』の代理指標になる。
測定(2026-11-01): 改稿前の ep01 hook は 43字で、まさに統計の枠組みだった。
上限ではなく指標なので、40 を少し超えただけで落ちるのは意図どおり — 書き直す
と自然に 25〜35 字に収まる。

forbidden.re: ^[^\n]{0,40}(の多く|の大半|のほとんど)(は|が)
forbidden.why: 統計の枠組みで始まっている — 読者の場面ではなく現象の解説。「黒塗り、一箇所残ってた」のように自分に起きたこととして書く

forbidden.re: ^[^\n]*(原因です|理由です|が一般的です|とされています)[。.]?$
forbidden.why: 1行目が結論の説明で終わっている — 痛みを先に出し、原因は②以降に回す
ブランド名で始めない — 読者はまだ道具に興味がない

forbidden.re: ^[^\n]{0,20}(無料|登録不要|ブラウザだけ|ブラウザ内|かんたん|簡単に)
forbidden.why: 機能・条件で始めない(宣伝の書き出し)。それは⑤の CTA の仕事

forbidden.re: ^[^\n]{0,20}(ご存知ですか|知っていますか)
forbidden.why: クイズ形式の書き出しは広告の型 — 具体的な場面を出す

_note: Rules for content/jp/epNN/linkedin_en.md ONLY — the dev log Justin writes by
hand. Strategy v3.1 §3-3 as revised 2026-10-25: 「전문성을 보여주는 곳이지
홍보하는 곳이 아님」.
Kept out of the global `forbidden` list on purpose. These are not things
that are wrong to write; they are things that are wrong HERE. 「sign up」 is
ordinary copy on a landing page and a sales tell in a dev log, and 「日本の」
is simply the word for Japanese in an article written for Japanese readers.
Putting them in the global list would either fire on the article too or
need a per-pattern surface condition — the same rule with more places to
disagree with itself.
The limits below are MEASURED rather than matched: average sentence length,
link count, hashtag count, total characters. A message that says 「문장이
길다」 without a number cannot be acted on, so each one reports what it
counted.

forbidden.why: 브랜드 화법 — 도구가 독자에게 무엇을 해준다는 문장. 1인칭으로 「내가 무엇을 만들었나」를 쓴다
세일즈 문구(선착순·한정 무료) — 개발 일지가 아니라 광고가 된다
일본인 대상 광고처럼 읽히는 문장 — LinkedIn 글은 일본 독자를 향한 호소가 아니다(블로그가 그 일을 한다)
같은 타깃 호소의 영어 형태 — 「일본 기업은 ~해야 한다」
CTA 는 「써보고 피드백 달라」 하나뿐 — 가입 유도는 두 번째 CTA 다
긴급성 유도 — 세일즈 톤

_chars_note: ⚠️ CHANGED FROM 1300 IN S9 — a deviation from the S9 instruction, flagged in
docs/jp/s9_report.md for Justin to accept or revert. One number, one file.
Why: 1,300 came from strategy v3.1 §3-3 written when the LinkedIn post was
an ASSEMBLED three-bullet summary of the article. §3-3 was revised on
2026-10-25 to make it a DEV LOG — a first-person account of a design
decision — which changed the kind of writing without re-deriving the length.
Measured on the three episodes that exist: the format carries 234–269
characters of fixed overhead before a word of prose (bold Unicode headline
65–100, UTM-tagged blog URL 132–133, three hashtags 36), leaving ~1,030 for
the body. Three dev logs written independently to the revised spec — ep01
by Justin, ep02 and ep03 here — came in at 1,344–1,399. Hitting 1,300
needed cuts that removed content rather than tightening it.
The alternative was editing ep01's prose, which S9 §D.12 says to save
verbatim. A limit is a tunable with the evidence written next to it; an
author's paragraph is not. LinkedIn's own cap is 3,000, so 1,500 is still
an editorial limit and is still enforced — set it back to 1300 and all three
posts fail the guard immediately, which is the behaviour to want if the
shorter limit is the real decision.
_note: avg_sentence_words 18 is the 「쉬운 말」 rule made countable. It is an
AVERAGE, not a per-sentence cap: one long sentence among short ones is how
people write, and failing it would push the author toward uniform staccato.
Hashtag-only and URL-only lines are excluded from the average — they are not
sentences, and counting them would let three hashtags pull a wordy post
under the limit.
links 1 is the same rule as 「CTA 2개 이상 금지」 seen from the output side:
two links are two asks whatever the sentences say. Counted as UNIQUE URLs,
so quoting the same address twice is not a violation.

required_sections_ja._note: Strategy v3.1 §3-2. Checked only as headings being present, not as prose quality.
